questions.q: What must you create before you can declare a table-valued parameter (TVP)?
options: A user-defined table type, with CREATE TYPE ... AS TABLE
A view over the target table
A scalar UDF that returns the row count
An INSTEAD OF trigger on the target table
questions.explain: A TVP's parameter type has to exist first as a reusable table type, defined with CREATE TYPE dbo.TypeName AS TABLE (columns).

questions.q: What modifier must a TVP parameter always have in a stored procedure's signature?
options: READONLY
OUTPUT
DEFAULT NULL
VARYING
questions.explain: A table-valued parameter can only be read from inside the procedure body, never modified — it must be declared READONLY.

questions.q: What problem does a TVP solve?
options: Passing a whole batch of rows into a stored procedure in a single call, instead of one call per row or a delimited string
Making a scalar UDF run faster
Allowing a trigger to roll back automatically
Replacing the need for a view entirely
questions.explain: Before TVPs, a batch of rows meant either many round-trips (one call per row) or a fragile delimited string parsed apart inside the procedure — a TVP replaces both with a real, typed table parameter.

questions.q: How do you call a procedure that takes a TVP, from T-SQL?
options: Declare a variable of the table type, INSERT rows into it, then pass that variable as the argument
Pass a comma-separated list of values directly as a string
Call the procedure once per row, passing one row's values each time
TVPs cannot be called from T-SQL, only from application code
questions.explain: DECLARE @Items dbo.SomeType; INSERT INTO @Items ...; then EXEC dbo.Proc @Items = @Items; sends every row in one call.

questions.q: Inside the procedure body, what can you do with a READONLY table-valued parameter?
options: SELECT from it and JOIN it like any other table, but not INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against it
Only pass it along unchanged to another procedure, nothing else
Modify its rows, as long as you don't change the row count
Nothing — it can only be inspected with a scalar UDF
questions.explain: A TVP behaves like any other table for read purposes — SELECT, JOIN, filter — but READONLY means you cannot write to it inside the procedure.
